title: the scratch proof holds on Windows: bare_temp_reach names paths with forward slashes and the stuck-sweep tooth locks its directory with an open handle
intention: bare_temp_reach reports each hit as a forward-slash path on every host, and the unsweepable-directory tooth holds an open file handle through the atexit sweep so the sweep fails and says so on Windows as chmod does on Linux.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: on Windows test_scratch.py reads 2 of 8 teeth failed: the reach tooth got ['proofs\\test_bare.py:2: ...'], the stuck-sweep tooth saw no could-not-remove line because chmod 0o500 did not stop the sweep; with the as_posix edit, an open handle in the child, and the exemption's as_posix it reads green twice
traces_to: Law 3: both causes measured by running the proof before and after; Law 8: a tooth that cannot fail on the host measures nothing, and the stuck-sweep tooth could not.
how: scratch.py line 238: py.relative_to(root).as_posix(). In test_scratch.py: the tooth opens a file under the stuck directory and keeps it referenced to interpreter teardown and cleans up with shutil.rmtree; the whole-repo scan's own-file exemption is built with as_posix so it still matches the posix reach names. The existing proof, red on Windows HEAD, is the red-first proof.
